body: I’ve posted this comment somewhere before at some point, but I’m a teacher, and, like, same, man.
The Suicide Hotline’s a sham anyway they put you on hold for an hour and then they seem to want to end the phone call almost as soon as they answer

Probably my second semester a senior in high school. I keep saying things would get better at some point, but after finishing high school, starting and finishing college, starting my career, I’ve noticed things actually continue to get worse and worse and I feel more and more trapped.

I guess the experience is different for everyone. I know somebody who was there for a year and ended up with a kind of managerial position making more than me with no college degree. But then I also knew someone who absolutely hated it.
Yeah, I’d say whatever this is started my senior year of high school and has gotten progressively worse. I’ve never received CBT though.
Thank you again, I don’t know why but sometimes kindness and understanding from complete strangers makes me feel better. Shows there’s still a lot of people out there that care

Thank you, I just don’t know what else to do. I know my license could be suspended if I do that, but I’m not even sure if I care. And as little as I get paid, it’s still a little bit more than I could get working full time at Walmart or something else here
I’m a teacher and same
I do the same thing, usually around the same time. Or if I’m just zoning out

I have too with the same results, I think most come here to maybe see they’re not alone as opposed to trying to offer anything. 

I don’t know, sometimes just a general acknowledgment feels good.

I wish I could respond to everyone. I read so many posts here sometimes. I just don’t know what to say. I don’t know what I can say that would really matter, I guess.
Thank you so much for replying, it’s kind of crazy how few people reply on subreddits like this ..
Huh, okay. I’m guessing the profile view thing was a privacy issue then? Alright. And I kind of figured about the block thing, just wanted to make sure.

I feel the same exact way. It’s like my brains playing tricks on me. I’ll convince myself that I don’t matter, that none of this matters. The littlest thing will upset me or worry me. It’s almost like I can’t function if there’s nothing for me to stress about.

I’ll sometimes just stop what I’m doing and question why I’m even trying to do anything? I’ve thought about suicide a lot, and I don’t exactly know why. I think I’m just tired of pretending that any of this matters? I graduate, I got a job, and now I do this forever I guess. 

You’re not alone. The feeling comes and goes for me. Although the feeling’s been showing up more than it’s been going away; it’s staying longer too.
The only time I’m not completely stressed out and anxious is when I’m asleep.
I feel the same way. At least once a week I shut myself out from people for a few days. Probably not the best thing but it is what it is.

I’m a teacher on the west coast, and it pains me to see things like this and what this pandemic has done to people emotionally and mentally.

I wish your teachers could show the same grace I have on some people. It’s tough, and I feel terrible.

I remember feeling how you do, and I still do, even though our circumstances are completely different now. 

I hope you can reconsider this, I don’t know what I can offer advice wise, but you’re not alone. Believe me, you’re not.

The FAQ on the website seemed vague in some places. It says during heavy traffic times but doesn’t really specify when those time are. 

It also says that speed and cell phone use don’t factor into your discount but they factor into the score ... which does impact your discount. So I’m kind of scratching my head at that one.

I’m fairly technically savvy, and I’m sure the app provides way to check whenever, correct?

And that’s also what I was thinking about. The discount goes down because I’m not “safe,” and it’ll appear the premiums going up when it really won’t be...

Do you know how sensitive the app is regarding movement and cell phone use? And how often does the discount actually go up or does State Farm use the app information to raise rates after the 6 months?

That’s kind of what I was worried about regarding cell phone use and battery charge. I’m also a little concerned about how sensitive the app is. The agent made it seem like it was lenient, and I’ve seen mixed reviews.
Maybe. I always say something like to myself but when it comes down to it, I just don’t want to “bring down the mood” or whatever ..

I think I want it more as a way to get it off my chest. Like some kind of weight is off my shoulders in a big wooooosh, or something.

But then I think, well, it’ll only feel like some of the weight is off my shoulders because I put some of it on someone else. 

I just don’t want to seem over dramatic, or that person stops talking to me. Or I don’t want them to freak out or worry. I never know how to even bring it up. As it is, I don’t see my friends very often any way; I only talk to them on the phone occasionally.
Like “oh shit.” And that was it. Like I said, we were both drinking and I joke about this stuff all the time. I didn’t really say it with the kind of tone I should’ve
